D14_runtime_use.A: binary plus an abstain signal; abstention must resolve to the conservative topology and must not stall agreement
D14_runtime_use.B: three-way; the boundary class must resolve to the conservative topology
D14_runtime_use.C: compare p_hat(x, COMPACT) against p_hat(x, LINE) and select the larger; ties and near-ties resolve to the conservative topology under a prospectively frozen margin
D14_runtime_use.requirement: every option must emit something a robot can rank locally with one scalar per candidate; C does this most directly

D15_safety_semantics.conservative_default: when the prediction is uncertain or the two candidates are within a frozen margin, the selector must keep the currently committed topology rather than initiate a transition
D15_safety_semantics.invariant: recoverability prediction NEVER overrides the frozen local safety projection
D15_safety_semantics.rationale: an unnecessary transition is itself a risk; holding is the conservative action
D15_safety_semantics.uncertainty_interface: uncertainty may only influence WHICH candidate is proposed, never whether the safety constraint is enforced

D28_boundary_handling_decision.question: should stochastic-boundary states be discarded, abstained, explicitly classified, or modelled?
D28_boundary_handling_decision.why_not_a_discrete_boundary_class: under all-success aggregation the class would be defined by R rather than by the state
D28_boundary_handling_decision.why_not_abstain_only: abstention needs its own supervision, which requires keeping the boundary events anyway
D28_boundary_handling_decision.why_not_deleted: the 59 TRAIN F9/LINE events are physically real, carry valid labels, and sit exactly where a candidate-conditioned selector has the most to learn. Deleting them is outcome-dependent filtering and removes the most informative region of the input space.

design_principle: the question answered here is 'what is the scientifically correct meaning of recoverability for a candidate topology under a stochastic disturbance distribution', NOT 'what makes 59/530 pass'

CRITICAL_FLAW_ADDRESSED.answer: it cannot. Deleting the mixed events removes exactly the supervision the abstention head would need. A workable version must RETAIN them with an explicit abstain label, at which point the design has become option B with a different name.
CRITICAL_FLAW_ADDRESSED.question: if ABSTAIN samples are removed from binary training, how will runtime know when to abstain?

options.definition_variant_1_FATAL_FLAW: the class boundary would be defined by R, not by physics. P(mixed) = 1 - p^R - (1-p)^R increases monotonically in R, so as R grows almost every event becomes 'boundary'. A class whose membership depends on the sampling budget is not a property of the state.
options.definition_variant_2: statistically justified classification, e.g. class by whether a confidence interval excludes a declared band
options.definition_variant_2_cost: requires per-event precision; R >= 27 for a +/-0.20 half-width
